feedback.problem:
$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]
$$

The Wronskian of the vector-valued functions given above is $W({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The Wronskian $W({x}_{1},{x}_{2})$ of two vector-valued functions 

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{11}(t) \\ {x}_{21}(t)\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{12}(t) \\ {x}_{22}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

is defined as

$$
W({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=det({x}_{1},{x}_{2})=|\begin{aligned}{x}_{11}(t) & {x}_{12}(t) \\ {x}_{21}(t) & {x}_{22}(t)\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, our Wronskian is

$$
\begin{aligned}W({x}_{1},{x}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}| \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡(3t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3t) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
